newsitem.title: INDIA: India Bharat Petroleum sets issue price.
newsitem.headline: India Bharat Petroleum sets issue price.

text.p: India's state-run refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) will price its forthcoming equity issue at 275 rupees a share, lead manager ICICI Securities and Finance Company Ltd (I-Sec) said on Tuesday.
The firm set its issue price on the lower end of a proposed price band of 270-320 rupees, an I-Sec official said.
The company hopes to raise over four billion rupees through an issue of 15 million shares, tentatively scheduled for October.
The proceeds of the issue would be deployed to part finance BPCL's capital expenditure programme which envisages an outlay of 57.2 billion rupees up to the year 1999/2000.
BPCL officials were not immediately available for comment.

I-Sec's R. Venkatraman said BPCL plans to reserve 20 percent of the share issue for domestic institutions, banks and mutual funds and another 20 percent for foreign institutional investors and NRIs (non-resident Indians). BPCL employees would be alloted 10 percent of the issue.
The issue would cut government's holding in BPCL to 60.18 percent from the current 66.20 percent.
Last month, BPCL officials said the firm planned an issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) next year which would further reduce the government holding to 51 percent.
BPCL refines 7.2 million tonnes of crude oil a year at its refinery near Bombay. It had a market share of 20.3 percent in the Indian petroleum market in 1995/96 (April-March).
